errorCodes.meaning: The oracle holds no group for this room: its principal is not a member, has not yet processed a welcome, or has left. An oracle whose principal was removed and not admitted again holds only prior memberships, and has no group to seal under: it answers `seal` with this code, and `open` by the requested epoch, as `unknownEpoch` describes. The framework defines no standard not-found code, so this one is declared.

The oracle cannot derive a key for the requested epoch. `details.reason` says why: `notDelivered` — the room has moved to an epoch whose commit has not reached the oracle yet, so retrying after it arrives may succeed, and `details.heldEpoch`, when present, is the latest epoch the oracle holds; `beyondChain` — the oracle's epoch chain reaches back only to `details.earliestEpoch`, and the file was sealed before the principal could read it, or before the room pruned its chain; `removed` — a commit the oracle processed removed its principal from the room's group at `details.removedAtEpoch`, and the requested epoch is at or after it and below the epoch the principal next joined at, if it has, so no later commit will make the key derivable and catching up will not help.

purpose.description: The purpose the request named, when it named one.

purposeNamed.description: Whether the request named a purpose. False when it named none where more than one is granted.

errorCodes.meaning: The request names a purpose that is not granted, or names none where more than one is granted — by the caller's authorization at the key holder or by the principal's authority over the room. The refusal discloses no content and is distinct from `permissionDenied`, which refuses access itself (VTI-ACL-104).

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

Purpose.description: What content is used for: a lowerCamelCase name registered in the VTI specification's purpose registry (Appendix H) — `personalisation`, `taskExecution`, `analytics`, `modelTraining` at the time of writing — or an absolute IRI naming a purpose defined elsewhere, such as a purpose of the W3C Data Privacy Vocabulary (`https://w3id.org/dpv#ServicePersonalisation`). Compared by exact string equality: a consumer MUST NOT treat a purpose it does not recognise as equal to any other, and grants only a request naming exactly a listed purpose (VTI-ACL-109). A registered name is never an IRI, because it contains no `:`.
Purpose.title: Purpose

RecordPurpose.description: The one purpose for which a caller will use room content a request discloses (VTI-ACL-103): a name registered in the VTI specification's purpose registry (`personalisation`, `taskExecution`, `analytics`, `modelTraining`) or an absolute IRI. Granted only as the caller's authority grants it — `any` grants every purpose but `modelTraining` — refused otherwise (`purposeNotGranted`), and recorded with the read. Distinct from `PermittedUse`, which is what a record's author permits and is a statement, not a grant.
RecordPurpose.title: RecordPurpose

epoch.description: The epoch the key was derived under. For `seal`, the room's current epoch, which the caller writes into the file's manifest; for `open`, the epoch requested.

key.description: The 32-byte file key, base64url without padding. Opens exactly one file. The caller holds it in memory for as long as the file is being sealed or opened and then discards it; it never stores, logs or forwards it.

schema.description: A caller asks the party holding its principal's room keys for the key of ONE file in a room: derived from the room's storage key for an epoch, bound to the room, the epoch and the file's identifier, and opening that file and nothing else.

epoch.description: The epoch the file key derives from, as FileManifest.epoch states it. REQUIRED for `open` and forbidden for `seal` — a rule over two members this schema does not express; the custodian refuses a violation with `malformedRequest`. A sealing caller never chooses the epoch: sealing under anything but the current one would produce a file members who joined later could not open, or one a removed member still could.

fileId.description: The file's identifier: 32 random bytes, base64url without padding, as in FileManifest.fileId. The salt of the derivation. For `seal` the caller mints it fresh and MUST NOT reuse it; for `open` it is read from the sealed record's file manifest.

purpose.description: `seal`: a key for a file about to be uploaded, derived under the room's CURRENT epoch, which the response names. `open`: a key for a file already in the room, derived under the epoch its manifest names.

purposeOfUse.description: OPTIONAL. The one purpose the caller will use the file the released key opens for (VTI-ACL-103), as `RecordPurpose` defines it. Named `purposeOfUse` because `purpose` already says which key is asked for. Bound only on `purpose: open`: a `seal` key is for content the caller is about to upload itself. A purpose not granted is refused with `purposeNotGranted`; may be omitted where exactly one purpose is granted, or `any`.

roomId.description: The room the file belongs to. Bound into the derivation, so a key released for one room cannot open a blob relocated from another.
